title: Variational Graph Autoencoder for Heterogeneous Information Networks with Missing and Inaccurate Attributes

problem.claim: Heterogeneous information networks contain multiple node and edge types, while practical settings may involve missing attributes, inaccurate attributes, and scarce node labels.

gap.claim: Most existing heterogeneous graph neural networks do not simultaneously address missing attributes, inaccurate attributes, and scarce node labels.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes GraMI, a generative self-supervised model for simultaneously handling missing attributes, inaccurate attributes, and scarce node labels in heterogeneous information networks.
GraMI learns node-level and attribute-level embeddings within a variational graph autoencoder encoder and reconstructs both links and attributes in its decoder.
GraMI generates an initial low-dimensional representation matrix for all nodes before reconstructing raw features for attributed nodes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments showing GraMI's superiority in handling heterogeneous information networks with missing and inaccurate attributes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heterogeneous information networks use multiple types of nodes and edges and have performed well in graph mining.
Existing heterogeneous graph neural networks are described as insufficient for jointly handling missing attributes, inaccurate attributes, and scarce node labels.
The paper introduces GraMI as a generative self-supervised model addressing these issues simultaneously.

GraMI initializes low-dimensional node representations, learns node- and attribute-level embeddings, reconstructs links and attributes, and uses generated representations to reconstruct attributed-node features.
The authors report extensive experiments indicating superior performance for HINs with missing and inaccurate attributes.
